exposure: Maternal pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) levels in the first trimester
outcome: Birth weight < 2 standard deviations below the mean
cohort: 961 pregnancies with PAPP-A levels < 0.3 MoM at the first-trimester combined screening between January 2009 and December 2012.
finding: The risks of aneuploidy, spontaneous abortion, preterm delivery, and small for gestational age newborn increased with decreasing PAPP-A levels.
mod_finding: The study found that women with extremely low pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) levels had increased rates of cesarean delivery.
birth_weight: Mentioned (< 2 standard deviations below the mean)
